title: The Fake Homecoming
premise: Noor Eriksen has spent senior year invisible, running an anonymous coding account that quietly exposes school corruption. When their best friend Amara vanishes days before homecoming, leaving behind a ring of keys and a half-deleted folder of board documents, Noor realizes Amara was digging into the same buried scandal — a decades-old land deal that explains why the district sold the community center where Noor's late grandmother taught. Following the keys through the school's forgotten spaces, Noor must choose between staying safe and going public with everything, including their own identity as the anonymous whistleblower. At the homecoming assembly, they expose the board's cover-up live, find Amara hiding in the old center's basement archives, and finally claim both their name and their inheritance: the truth.
about_author: Cyrus Okonkwo is a former high school debate coach who writes stories about teenagers who refuse to be quiet. He lives in Ohio with a rescue dog named Semaphore and an unhealthy collection of mechanical keyboards.

chapters.title: Locker Shut
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. We meet Noor mid-senior-year: perfect grades, zero social footprint, secretly running the anonymous account 'HallMonitor' that leaks school board records. A tender scene with best friend Amara, who teases that Noor will graduate without anyone knowing their name. Emotional beat: the comfort — and loneliness — of invisibility.

chapters.title: The Keys She Left
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Amara misses three days of school; her texts stop mid-sentence. Police call it a runaway case, but Noor finds a bag in Amara's locker containing seven unlabeled keys and a corrupted flash drive. The chapter ends with Noor recognizing one key: it opens the demolished community center's maintenance door. Beat: fear sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Seven Doors
chapters.summary: Noor's POV, alternating with flashbacks to Amara's last week reconstructed from her recovered chat logs. Noor tests each key against school maps, discovering doors to rooms officially closed since the district's 2019 consolidation. Each room holds traces of Amara's investigation. Beat: dread — Amara wasn't paranoid; she was being followed.

chapters.title: The Man Who Sold the Center
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Research reveals board president Dale Voss brokered the sale of the community center — where Noor's grandmother ran a free coding program — to a developer with hidden ties to Voss himself. Noor posts an anonymous thread and gets an immediate, chilling reply from someone who knows details only Amara knew. Beat: grief curdling into anger.

chapters.title: Homecoming Court
chapters.summary: POV shifts to Priya Chandrasekaran, student council treasurer and reluctant homecoming chair, who notices budget line items funneled to a shell company. She suspects HallMonitor is a student and starts narrowing candidates. Her path crosses Noor's when she catches them photographing board minutes. Beat: wary alliance forming between two people who trust no one.

chapters.title: What Grandmother Kept
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. In their grandmother's belongings, Noor finds letters showing she fought the sale before her death — and that Amara had contacted her old lawyer weeks ago. The keys fit a pattern: they trace the paper trail physically through the building. Noor realizes Amara left them a map on purpose. Beat: inheritance reframed — not money, but a fight.

chapters.title: Locked In
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Noor and Priya follow the final key into the sub-basement archive during the homecoming dance setup and are locked in by someone with a master key. Trapped for hours, they decrypt Amara's drive together and find signed documents proving Voss falsified the appraisal. Priya deduces Noor is HallMonitor. Beat: terror, then the relief of being fully known.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Voss corners Noor privately: full scholarship money, Amara's record quietly cleaned up, in exchange for the drive and silence. He implies Amara took a similar deal and chose to disappear rather than comply. Noor pretends to consider it while recording him. Beat: temptation and moral clarity colliding.

chapters.title: Assembly
chapters.summary: Priya's POV, climax. At the homecoming assembly, Priya hijacks the AV feed and Noor steps onstage — unmasking themselves as HallMonitor, playing the recording, and projecting the forged appraisal to the whole school. Chaos erupts; Voss is escorted out as a state investigator, tipped by Amara's lawyer, walks in. Beat: catharsis at maximum volume.

chapters.title: Basement Light On
chapters.summary: Noor's POV, resolution. Following the last clue — a text sent during the assembly — Noor finds Amara alive in the community center basement, where she'd been hiding with the lawyer while gathering testimony, too scared to surface until Voss fell. The friends reconcile amid anger and relief. The center is slated for restoration under Noor's grandmother's name. Beat: identity claimed, home reclaimed.
